summary:
Orbitone is an astronaut wellbeing platform designed to support physical and emotional health during long space missions. It combines simulated health telemetry, daily mood check-ins, wellbeing trends, and safe AI-generated daily missions in one simple interface. Astronauts can monitor changes in sleep, energy, stress, mood, and social connection over time.

The AI uses the latest available data to provide three short, personalized, non-medical activities, such as taking a brief rest, organizing the next task, or connecting with a crew member. All sensitive data is processed securely, and the system avoids diagnosis or treatment advice.

Orbitone addresses the challenge by making health monitoring easier to understand and act on. It is important because small, timely actions can help astronauts maintain healthy routines, reduce isolation, and stay focused during demanding missions.
details:
Orbitone is an astronaut wellbeing platform that brings physical health monitoring, emotional check-ins, trends, and AI-assisted daily missions into one clear experience. The system receives simulated telemetry such as heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep duration, steps, and body temperature. Astronauts can also complete a short daily check-in about mood, stress, energy, and social connection. The platform combines these inputs to show health and mood scores, highlight changes over time, and suggest three short, safe actions for the day.

The frontend communicates only with our backend. The backend stores the data, calculates scores and trends, checks whether information is missing or outdated, and decides when the AI service can be used safely. Gemini considers the latest approved data and bounded trends to select suitable missions from a controlled set of low-risk activities. It cannot diagnose medical conditions, recommend treatment, or access private journal and symptom notes. If the AI is offline, exceeds its quota, or returns an invalid response, the backend uses a deterministic fallback so the application continues working.

We developed the frontend with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and React Three Fiber. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Alembic, Docker, and a separate telemetry simulator. The AI service was developed with Node.js and the Gemini API. We also created automated tests for API validation, privacy rules, AI responses, fallback behavior, scoring, persistence, and frontend data handling. GitHub branches and shared API contracts allowed the frontend, backend, and AI modules to be developed independently and integrated safely.

One of Orbitone’s creative features is the 1Garden. Each crew has a shared virtual garden, and every astronaut is represented by one personal plant. The plant’s condition provides a simple visual reflection of the astronaut’s general wellbeing progress without revealing private health readings. Astronaut profiles display their name, crew identity, and plant. The demo astronaut can visit the garden, view the plants of other crew members, and see how the team is doing at a glance. In the prototype, one astronaut acts as the demo user, while the other crew profiles are preloaded to demonstrate the shared experience. This creates a gentle sense of connection and encourages crew members to notice and support one another during long missions.

Orbitone is designed to turn complex wellbeing data into understandable and achievable actions. The intended impact is to help astronauts recognize changes early, maintain healthy routines, reduce feelings of isolation, and stay focused during demanding missions. We considered privacy, medical safety, missing data, limited connectivity, AI reliability, accessibility, and the realities of long-duration space travel throughout the design process.
